extracted.intended_audience: general literate readers of The Spectator; readers interested in manners, morals, and literary style
extracted.subtask_description: Short early-18th-century Spectator essays giving prescriptive advice and observations about personal conduct, writing style (egotism), social negotiation, and informal rules (e.g., a Widow-Club's tactics for managing suitors and husbands).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid egotism / speaking of oneself
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the Tenour of his Discourse be what it will upon this Subject, it generally proceeds from Vanity. Never to speak of himself, unless there be something very considerable in his Character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay criticises authors who write in the first person (eg Tully, Montagne) and memoir-writers; it notes that prefaces often display unnecessary self-information. Exception: in works of humour or when writing under a fictitious personage, speaking of oneself may give diversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid trivial preface disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Many modern Prefaces savour very strongly of the Egotism. Every insignificant Author fancies it of Importance to the World, to know that he writ his Book in the Country, that he did it to pass away some of his idle Hours, that it was published at the Importunity of Friends...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such informations are presented as not improving to the reader; authors are advised not to burden prefaces with irrelevant personal circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not repine at your own misfortunes; accept your lot
rubrics_metrics.description: Never to repine at my own Misfortunes, or to envy the Happiness of another, since it is impossible for any Man to form a right Judgment of his Neighbour's Sufferings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on the vision of exchanging human calamities: switching others' misfortunes often produces worse outcomes; therefore one should be content with, and bear, one's own share rather than covet another's.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate patience to bear calamities
rubrics_metrics.description: PATIENCE ... had no sooner placed her self by the Mount of Sorrows, but, what I thought very remarkable, the whole Heap sunk to such a Degree... She afterwards returned every Man his own proper Calamity, and teaching him how to bear it in the most commodious Manner, he marched off with it contentedly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patience is presented as a practical virtue that reduces the burden of suffering and enables people to bear their own afflictions contentedly rather than seeking ill-considered exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value sincerity; distrust double-tongued politeness
rubrics_metrics.description: They call thee and thy Subjects Barbarians, because we speak what we mean... Truth they call Barbarity, and Falsehood Politeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given (excessive apologies, insincere offers of service, ostentatious civility that conceals unhelpful behaviour) are used to warn readers that social politeness can mask dishonesty; this undermines trust and negotiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware insincere compliments and false assurances when negotiating
rubrics_metrics.description: When I go to see the King's Scribe, I am generally told that he is not at home, tho' perhaps I saw him go into his House almost the very Moment before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text treats such behaviour as a practical impediment to business; readers are cautioned to give little credit to professions of civility that are not backed by action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Widow-Club principal rule: praise single life to deter marriage
rubrics_metrics.description: The principal Rule, by which the whole Society are to govern themselves is this, To cry up the Pleasures of a single Life upon all Occasions, in order to deter the rest of their Sex from Marriage, and engross the whole Male World to themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as the Club's political/social aim: members are to promote singleness publicly as part of their strategy to attract and monopolize men.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for vetting suitors (Widow-Club)
rubrics_metrics.description: They are obliged, when any one makes Love to a Member of the Society, to communicate his Name, at which Time the whole Assembly sit upon his Reputation, Person, Fortune, and good Humour;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Club collectively evaluates any suitor by reputation, appearance, fortune, and temper; if deemed suitable, they collaborate to secure him. This is given as an explicit protocol for assessing and coordinating action on lovers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Widow-Club doctrine: not to give him his head at first
rubrics_metrics.description: Not to give him his Head at first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among the universal doctrines for managing a husband: initial restraint on husband's autonomy to secure the wife's influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Widow-Club doctrine: limit freedoms and familiarities
rubrics_metrics.description: Not to allow him too great Freedoms and Familiarities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aimed at preserving control and reserve in the early phase of marriage/relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Widow-Club doctrine: be treated as experienced, not a raw girl
rubrics_metrics.description: Not to be treated by him like a raw Girl, but as a Woman that knows the World.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages presenting oneself as worldly-wise to command respect and authority in the relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Widow-Club doctrine: preserve one's former figure/status
rubrics_metrics.description: Not to Lessen anything of her former Figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice to maintain established appearance, reputation, or social advantages after remarriage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Widow-Club doctrine: praise deceased husband's virtues to the successor
rubrics_metrics.description: To celebrate the Generosity, or any other Vertue, of a deceased Husband, which she would recommend to his Successor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tactic to make the new husband think favorably of the widow's past and to create contrast that benefits her position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Widow-Club doctrine: remove husband's old friends and servants
rubrics_metrics.description: To turn away all his old Friends and Servants, that she may have the Dear Man to her self.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A method to isolate the husband from previous influences and secure exclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Widow-Club doctrine: disinherit undutiful children of former wife
rubrics_metrics.description: To make him disinherit the undutiful Children of any former Wife.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A financial/legal tactic to consolidate property/control in favor of the current wife.

rubrics_metrics.name: Widow-Club doctrine: do not trust his affection until he transfers assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Never to be thoroughly convinced of his Affection, till he has made over to her all his Goods and Chattels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cynical rule treating material transfer as the proof of genuine commitment; presented as part of the Club's sardonic strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid passing off common jokes as original (conversational egotism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Those empty conceited Fellows, who repeat as Sayings of their own, or some of their particular Friends, several Jests which were made before they were born...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommends remedying this affectation by reading collections (Oxford and Cambridge Jests) so one recognizes prior circulation and stops claiming others' witticisms as original.
